notes: Rust std (f64/f32 methods, integer constants) where it matches Go; first-party ports of Go's algorithms (from FreeBSD msun, bit-identical to Go's portable code) for everything whose std result differs from Go's: trigonometry, inverse trigonometry, hyperbolics, exp/log families, pow, hypot, cbrt, erf, gamma and Bessel; NaN() is Go's bit pattern 0x7FF8000000000001. int is i64 and uint is usize (the surface is 64-bit). The differential compares bit patterns against an amd64 Go oracle where one can run (Go on arm64 fuses x*y+z, which changes the last bits of Go's own code; a native arm64 oracle is accepted with wider tolerances). Subnormal arguments of log-based functions and exp near overflow are skipped, because Go's amd64 assembly is inaccurate there. Every result is bit-identical except the symbols marked platform-float, which inherit the last-bit differences of Go's platform-specific assembly Exp. NaN payloads are not compared.

Cosh.note: Go's Exp is assembly on amd64 (with a different path on CPUs with FMA) and arm64, and its last bit differs between them and from Go's portable algorithm, which is what this crate ports (bit-identical to Go's math/exp.go). Against an amd64 Go without FMA the result differs by up to 2 ULP; it is Go's formula over Exp. Special values match. Go's own last bits differ between amd64 (with and without FMA) and arm64 assembly; results are within Go's documented accuracy and special values match exactly. Implementation-defined, like unstable sort order.
